description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The Child project will also deliver socio-economic benefits, including:Enhanced skills and green job opportunities: The project will build skills related to Best Management Practices (BMPs) in agroecology. This will create new green job opportunities, empowering individuals with the knowledge and abilities to engage in sustainable agricultural practices. This will be reported under the indirect beneficiaries in Core Indicator 11. Endorsed land use regulation: This project will support the development and endorsement of land regulations and their associated instruments. These regulations will facilitate access to more sustainable economic activities and promote the integrated management of water resources. This will be reported under component 2.By promoting sustainable land use and water management, the project aims to reduce the risks associated with freshwater resources, ensuring their availability and quality for future generations. Relevant literature emphasizes the substantial socio-economic advantages of initiatives to promote land-use policies and adopt sustainable farming BMPs. These efforts have demonstrated the ability to: ü Contribute to local economic development – Land use regulations will facilitate access to more sustainable economic activities and promote the integrated management of water resources. ü Boost Green Economy—The project will create new green job opportunities and empower individuals with the knowledge and skills to engage in sustainable agricultural practices. ü Increase Agricultural Productivity—The integration of sustainable agricultural techniques into land-use policies has resulted in yield increases of 15-25%, bolstering food security and economic resilience. ü Improve Food Security – In Bolivia, the CRIAR project enhanced food security for participants by 32%, significantly lowering the risk of food shortages for households. ü Increase Household Income – Voucher-based initiatives have led to notable income growth, including a 36% increase in earnings for Bolivian farmers and a 12% rise in income for livestock producers in the Dominican Republic. ü Enhance Resource Efficiency and Sustainability – Those who adopted innovative technologies experienced productivity gains of up to 92%, resulting in more efficient resource use and sustainable farming practices. ü Encourage Economic Diversification—Farmers transitioned to higher-value crops, broadening market access and promoting long-term profitability. The IDB has effectively implemented voucher-based strategies across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), achieving four of these seven outcomes. As part of its third and second components, the project expects to deliver similar socio-economic benefits through land use planning, technical support, and farm planning processes.
To contribute to reduce water contamination and the risk of marine hypoxia in Parita Bay in Panama.
